newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma papers launch fresh attack on Aung San Suu Kyi.
newsitem.headline: Burma papers launch fresh attack on Aung San Suu Kyi.

text.p: Burmese opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi may be accused of political crimes for her outspoken attacks on the military government, state-run newspapers said on Wednesday.
"In the not too distant future she will be accused as a political criminal," said a commentary in all three official newspapers.
"This is because her decisions and wrong deeds have led to many events which cannot be redeemed politically."

Burma's media is tightly controlled by the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC), which has ignored Suu Kyi's repeated calls for dialogue since her release from six years of house arrest in July 1995.
Suu Kyi has also condemned human rights abuses in Burma and urged foreign investors to withold funds until the SLORC agrees to work towards democracy and improve its human rights' record.
The newspapers accused Suu Kyi and the opposition National League for Democracy (NLD) of using foreign media to attack the government.
The commentary said calls for foreigners not to invest in Burma would hurt the Burmese people, not the government.
"Therefore, it is high time the people realise ... that the selfish acts of the National League for Democracy could bring about ill effects," it said.
The National League for Democracy was "neither aware of the prevailing situation nor does it have any experience to rule the country and this is a very dreadful and frightening thing".

It said Suu Kyi lacked the qualities necessary to lead a party in government, adding that "her stubborn spirit, immature political experience, dictatorial qualities and feminine nature" would lead to "disintegration of the country or the government and disunity among the people".
